plugin_desc: SNMP monitoring template for Huawei switch. It reports uptime, CPU utilization, memory utilization, temperature, fan, power supply status, optical modules, interface traffic, voltage, and power (enterprise PEN 2011).
name: Switch

metrics.name: device_cpu_usage
metrics.description: Per-entity CPU utilization of the Huawei device control plane (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityCpuUsage), normalized to a 0-100 percentage. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. Sustained high CPU usage can indicate control-plane overload, routing instability, or attack traffic, and may lead to slow management response or packet processing delays.

metrics.name: device_memory_usage
metrics.description: Per-entity memory utilization of the Huawei device (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityMemUsage), reported directly as a 0-100 percentage. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. High memory usage may indicate memory leaks, oversized routing/MAC/ARP tables, or insufficient capacity, and can cause instability or failed allocations.

metrics.name: device_temperature_celsius
metrics.description: This metric reports the temperature reading of each Huawei hardware sensor (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityTemperature), in degrees Celsius. Abnormally high temperatures may indicate fan failure, blocked airflow, or excessive ambient heat, and can trigger thermal protection or hardware damage if left unaddressed.

metrics.name: device_voltage_volts
metrics.description: Per-entity input voltage of the Huawei switch (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityVoltage). The device reports millivolts; the query divides by 1000 to display volts. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName, sharing hwEntityStateTable with CPU/memory/temperature. Distinct from optical-module voltage device_optical_voltage (hwEntityOpticalVoltage). Values outside the rated range may indicate unstable power and hardware risk.

metrics.name: device_fan_state
metrics.description: Operational state of each installed Huawei switch cooling fan (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityFanState). On-wire INTEGER is normal(1)/abnormal(2). The query keeps only present(1) rows so empty slots are not treated as faults. Dimension descr is hwEntityFanSlot.

metrics.name: device_fan_speed
metrics.description: Fan speed of each installed Huawei switch cooling fan (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityFanSpeed), reported as a percentage of full speed. Shares hwFanStatusTable with device_fan_state; dimension descr is hwEntityFanSlot. The query keeps only present(1) rows so empty slots are dropped. Persistently high speed can indicate thermal compensation; a drop toward 0% with a healthy state may still mean a stalled rotor.

metrics.name: device_fan_present
metrics.description: Presence of each Huawei switch cooling fan (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityFanPresent). On-wire INTEGER is present(1)/absent(2), not 0/1. Absent means the slot is empty or the fan tray was pulled. Dimension descr is hwEntityFanSlot.

metrics.name: device_psu_state
metrics.description: Operational state of each installed Huawei switch power supply (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityPwrState). On-wire INTEGER is supply(1)/notSupply(2)/sleep(3)/unknown(4), not a binary normal/abnormal. The query keeps only present(1) rows so empty slots are not treated as faults. sleep(3) is a valid redundant-PSU energy-saving state. Dimension descr is hwEntityPwrSlot.

metrics.name: device_psu_present
metrics.description: Presence of each Huawei switch power supply (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityPwrPresent). On-wire INTEGER is present(1)/absent(2), not 0/1. Absent means the slot is empty or the module was pulled. Dimension descr is hwEntityPwrSlot.

metrics.name: device_psu_current_mA
metrics.description: Output current of each installed Huawei switch power supply (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityPwrCurrent), in milliamperes (mA) as reported on the wire, not amperes. Shares hwPwrStatusTable with device_psu_state; the query keeps only present(1) rows so empty slots are dropped. Dimension descr is hwEntityPwrSlot. Divide by 1000 to read amperes. A sudden drop toward 0 mA on a present, supplying module can indicate a failing PSU or lost load path.

metrics.name: device_psu_voltage_mV
metrics.description: Output voltage of each installed Huawei switch power supply (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityPwrVoltage), in millivolts (mV) as reported on the wire, not volts. Shares hwPwrStatusTable with device_psu_state; the query keeps only present(1) rows so empty slots are dropped. Dimension descr is hwEntityPwrSlot. Divide by 1000 to read volts. Values far from the module's expected rail indicate unstable supply and hardware risk.

metrics.name: device_psu_rated_power_watts
metrics.description: Rated power of each installed Huawei switch power-supply module (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityPwrPower), in watts. This is the module nameplate rating, not chassis instantaneous used power (device_power_used). Shares hwPwrStatusTable with device_psu_state; the query keeps only present(1) rows. Dimension descr is hwEntityPwrSlot. Summing present modules gives the installed PSU budget.

metrics.name: device_power_used
metrics.description: Chassis-level used power of the Huawei switch (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwDevicePowerInfoUsedPower), in watts. Rising used power against a stable total budget indicates growing load or a hardware inefficiency.

metrics.name: device_power_total
metrics.description: Chassis-level total power capacity of the Huawei switch (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwDevicePowerInfoTotalPower), in watts. Used as the denominator when judging how close the chassis is to its power budget.

metrics.name: device_entity_board_power
metrics.description: Board power consumption of each Huawei switch entity (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityBoardPower), in watts. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. Distinct from ENERGYMNGT milliwatt series device_board_current_power_mw / device_board_rated_power_mw. Unexpected rise can indicate a failing board, abnormal traffic load, or a cooling problem that increases power draw.

metrics.name: device_energy_current_power_mw
metrics.description: Instantaneous chassis energy of the Huawei switch (hwCurrentPower), in milliwatts (mW). Divide by 1000 to display watts. Distinct from device_power_used, which is chassis used power in watts from hwDevicePowerInfoUsedPower.

metrics.name: device_energy_average_power_mw
metrics.description: Period-average chassis energy of the Huawei switch (hwAveragePower), in milliwatts (mW). Divide by 1000 to display watts. Distinct from device_power_used (watts).

metrics.name: device_energy_rated_power_mw
metrics.description: Rated chassis energy of the Huawei switch (hwRatedPower), in milliwatts (mW). Divide by 1000 to display watts. Distinct from device_power_total, which is chassis total power in watts from hwDevicePowerInfoTotalPower.

metrics.name: device_board_current_power_mw
metrics.description: Instantaneous energy of each Huawei switch board (hwBoardCurrentPower), in milliwatts (mW). Divide by 1000 to display watts. Dimension hwBoardName is the board name. Distinct from chassis watts metrics device_power_used / device_power_total and from entity watts metric device_entity_board_power (hwEntityBoardPower).

metrics.name: device_board_rated_power_mw
metrics.description: Rated energy of each Huawei switch board (hwBoardRatedPower), in milliwatts (mW). Divide by 1000 to display watts. Dimension hwBoardName is the board name.

metrics.name: device_optical_rx_power
metrics.description: Per-module SFP/optical receive power in dBm (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityOpticalRxPower). Campus switches report µW on the wire (MIB text often says dBm×100). Telegraf stores raw µW and this query converts with 10*log10(µW/1000), dropping <=0 and the 2147483647 invalid sentinel. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. A dropping RX level is an early sign of fiber attenuation, dirty optics, or a failing peer transmitter.

metrics.name: device_optical_tx_power
metrics.description: Per-module SFP/optical transmit power in dBm (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityOpticalTxPower). Campus switches report µW on the wire (MIB text often says dBm×100). Telegraf stores raw µW and this query converts with 10*log10(µW/1000), dropping <=0 and the 2147483647 invalid sentinel. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. An abnormally low TX level indicates a failing laser/optic rather than fiber attenuation alone.

metrics.name: device_optical_temperature
metrics.description: Temperature of each Huawei switch optical module (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityOpticalTemperature), in degrees Celsius. The query drops the 2147483647 invalid sentinel. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. High module temperature accelerates laser aging and can precede optical power failure.

metrics.name: device_optical_bias
metrics.description: Laser bias current of each Huawei switch optical module (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityOpticalBiasCurrent), in microamperes (µA) as reported on the wire. The query drops the 2147483647 invalid sentinel. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. Drift away from the normal range is an early sign of a failing transmitter.

metrics.name: device_optical_voltage
metrics.description: Supply voltage of each Huawei switch optical module (HUAWEI-ENTITY-EXTENT-MIB hwEntityOpticalVoltage). The device reports millivolts; the query divides by 1000 to display volts and drops the 2147483647 invalid sentinel. Dimension descr is entPhysicalName. Distinct from per-entity device_voltage_volts (hwEntityVoltage). Out-of-range voltage can cause unstable optics.

metrics.name: device_stack_member_role
metrics.description: Role of each Huawei iStack / CE stack member (HUAWEI-STACK-MIB hwMemberStackRole). On-wire INTEGER is master(1)/standby(2)/slave(3). Dimension descr is hwMemberCurrentStackId.

metrics.name: device_stack_port_state
metrics.description: Operational state of each Huawei iStack / CE stack port (HUAWEI-STACK-MIB hwStackPortStatus). On-wire INTEGER is up(1)/down(2). Down means the physical stack port cannot carry stack control or forwarding, which can split the stack or force a suboptimal topology.

metrics.name: device_css_member_role
metrics.description: Role of each Huawei CSS member (HUAWEI-STACK-MIB hwCssMemberRole). On-wire INTEGER is master(1)/standby(2)/slave(3)/single(4)/unknown(10). Dimension descr is hwCssMemberFrameId.

metrics.name: device_css_port_state
metrics.description: Operational state of each Huawei CSS port (HUAWEI-STACK-MIB hwCssPortOperStatus). On-wire INTEGER is down(0)/up(1), not the stack-port up(1)/down(2) encoding. Using a >1 threshold would never fire. Dimension descr is hwCssPortName.

metrics.name: device_mlag_port_state
metrics.description: Operational state of each Huawei M-LAG member port (HUAWEI-M-LAG-MIB hwPortState). On-wire INTEGER is down(0)/up(1). Down means this M-LAG member cannot forward in the dual-homed bundle. Dimension descr is hwMlagPortName. Empty when M-LAG is not enabled.

metrics.name: device_mlag_member_heartbeat
metrics.description: Heartbeat of the local Huawei M-LAG member (HUAWEI-M-LAG-MIB hwLocalHeartBeatState). On-wire INTEGER is ok(1)/lost(2). Lost means the dual-active control channel between M-LAG peers is down. Dimension descr is hwLocalNodeId. Consistency-check objects in this MIB are traps and are not polled.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCInOctets
metrics.description: This metric indicates the average rate of bytes received over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCInOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifInOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: interface_ifHCOutOctets
metrics.description: This metric calculates the average rate of bytes sent over the past 5 minutes, measured in bytes per second, from the 64-bit IF-MIB ifHCOutOctets counter (ifXTable). The 64-bit counter avoids the rapid wrap of the 32-bit ifOutOctets on high-speed switch ports, keeping the rate accurate.

metrics.name: snmp_uptime
metrics.description: This metric indicates the uptime of the device since the last restart. By monitoring the uptime, network administrators can understand the stability and reliability of the device and identify potential reboot or failure issues.
